quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money total is computed with floats inside render, from unrounded prices, so the total can disagree with the lines shown
evidence: Prices are accepted with any number of decimals (app.js:18-19), displayed per line with toFixed(2) (app.js:8), summed unrounded here, and the same unrounded lines are POSTed (app.js:26). The pricing rule lives in the view function with no separate pure function or test. Traced from the JS toFixed spec (ties pick the larger n).
failing_case: Add two lines, each client 'a', qty 1, price 0.125. Each line renders as `1 × 0.13` (toFixed(2) of 0.125 is '0.13'), but the total is (0.125+0.125).toFixed(2) = '0.25', not 0.26. The invoice shows lines that add to 0.26 and a total of 0.25. The server receives price 0.125.
remediation: Move money maths into one pure, tested function that works in integer minor units, round the unit price once at input (reject more than 2 decimals), and have the view and the POST body use the same rounded values.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send has no try/catch and no success feedback: an offline failure is silent, and a success looks the same
evidence: fetch rejects on network failure; there is no catch, so the handler ends in an unhandled rejection and the user sees nothing. On success only `sentCount += 1` runs (app.js:28); sentCount is never read or displayed, and the lines stay in the list. Traced.
failing_case: Go offline (or the server drops the connection), add a line, click Send. fetch throws, the console shows an unhandled rejection, the page shows nothing. A user cannot tell this from a successful send, and on a real success the page is also unchanged, so they click again and, after 1 s, send a duplicate.
remediation: Wrap the request in try/catch/finally, show an in-page status (role=status) for sending, sent and failed with a next step, and clear or lock the lines after a confirmed success.

title: Double-send guard is a one-second timer, not an in-flight lock, so a slow request can be sent twice
evidence: tooSoon() (guards.js:21-26) only compares Date.now() with the last click. app.js:24-29 awaits fetch with no pending flag and does not disable the Send button. Traced.
failing_case: Click Send on a connection where POST /api/invoices takes more than 1 s (or the user clicks again after 1.1 s because nothing happened). tooSoon() returns false the second time, so a second POST with the same lines goes out while the first is pending. The server creates two invoices for the same lines. Also, a click within 1 s of a failed send is silently swallowed, so a quick retry does nothing.
remediation: Hold a `sending` flag for the life of the request (disable the button in a try/finally) and send an idempotency key with the POST so the server can drop duplicates.

title: Whitespace-only client passes `required`, is trimmed to empty, and is added as a line with no client
evidence: The browser's `required` (index.html:14) only rejects an empty string, so '   ' is accepted. The value is trimmed here and never rechecked before lines.push (app.js:20). Traced.
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, qty 1, price 5, press Add line. A line with client '' is added, rendered as an empty link with no accessible name, and sent to the server in the invoice.
remediation: Check the trimmed client is non-empty before pushing and show an inline error; set the field value to the trimmed text.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently: the Add line button appears to do nothing
evidence: The early return has no message, no aria-invalid and no focus move. The price field uses inputmode=decimal (index.html:18), which on many locales' keyboards types a comma; Number('12,50') is NaN so the line is rejected. Traced.
failing_case: Type client 'Acme', qty 2, price '12,50', press Add line: nothing is added and nothing is said. Same for qty '1.5', qty '0' or an empty price.
remediation: Parse price through one normaliser (accepting a decimal comma), and on rejection show an inline error tied to the field (aria-describedby, aria-invalid) saying what is wrong and the accepted format.

title: A mistaken line cannot be removed or edited, and the form is not reset after adding
evidence: The only operations on `lines` are push (this line) and reading. There is no remove or edit control in index.html. Inputs keep their values after a successful add. Traced.
failing_case: Add a line with a wrong price, notice, and look for a way to delete it: none. The only way to fix it is to reload, which discards every other line. Pressing Enter twice adds the same line twice.
remediation: Add a per-line Remove button (with an accessible name that includes the client), clear and refocus the form after a successful add.

title: An empty invoice can be sent
evidence: Nothing between the click and the fetch checks lines.length. With no lines the body is `[]`. Traced.
failing_case: Open the page, click Send invoice without adding a line. POST /api/invoices is sent with body `[]`; nothing tells the user it was a no-op or an error.
remediation: Disable Send while there are no lines, and reject an empty list before the request with a visible message.

title: Void button does nothing, with no message, for users who are not admins; network failure on void is also silent
evidence: The button is always enabled (index.html:24). The user object in app.js:2 has roles viewer and billing, so every click returns here with no output. fetch at app.js:33 has no catch and no success message. Traced.
failing_case: As user 'sam' (viewer, billing) click Void invoice: nothing changes, no text, no disabled state. A second case: as an admin, go offline and click Void: unhandled rejection, no message.
remediation: Disable or hide the control when canVoid is false (with the reason in text), and wrap the request in try/catch with a visible, announced success or failure message.

title: Destructive Void has no confirmation, no undo, and can be fired repeatedly
evidence: A single click on a plain button goes straight to the POST. There is no confirm step, no in-flight lock (tooSoon is used only on Send), and the request names no invoice. Traced.
failing_case: An admin who misclicks Void next to Send voids the invoice immediately; repeated clicks send repeated void requests.
remediation: Add a confirm step that names the invoice and states what happens, lock the button during the request, and offer undo where the API allows.

title: Void permission is enforced only in the browser, against a hard-coded user object
evidence: canVoid reads `user`, a constant defined in app.js:2. The void request (app.js:33) carries no identity or invoice id. The server is not in the payload, so whether it re-checks the role is unknown. Inferred requirement: 'Only admins may void an invoice' (guards.js:9).
failing_case: A signed-in viewer opens the console and runs `fetch('/api/invoices/void', {method:'POST'})`, or edits `user.roles` to include 'admin'. The client check is bypassed. If the server does not enforce the role itself, a non-admin voids an invoice.

requirement.why: The comment on canVoid says only admins may void; the check exists only client-side in this payload.

remediation: Enforce the role on the server for /api/invoices/void, take the user from the session, and send the invoice id in the request. Keep the client check only to hide the button.

title: Each line's client name is a dead link (href="#") that adds a tab stop and jumps the page to the top
evidence: The anchor has no handler anywhere in app.js and no real target. The title attribute repeats the link text. Traced.
failing_case: Tab through the page after adding three lines: three focusable 'links' that, when activated, change the URL to `#` and scroll to the top, doing nothing else. Screen readers announce them as links.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text, or give it a real destination or a button with a real action. Drop the duplicate title.

title: Price parsing via Number() accepts 'Infinity', '1e400', '0x10' and 1e21-scale values
evidence: Number('Infinity') > 0 is true, and Number('0x10') is 16. validQuantity (guards.js:16) also allows arbitrarily long digit strings. Traced.
failing_case: Type Infinity in Unit price, qty 1: the line is added, the total renders 'Infinity', and JSON.stringify sends null for the price in the POST body.
remediation: Parse price with a strict decimal pattern (digits, one separator, at most two decimals) and cap quantity and price to a sane maximum.
